study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Sun et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2025
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissecting heterogeneity in major depressive disorder via normative model-driven subtyping of functional brain networks

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Data were obtained from the REST-meta-MDD project provided by the DIRECT consortium. This is a publicly accessible multi-site resting-state fMRI dataset. Site 4 and Site 25 were excluded (Site 4 duplicated Site 14; Site 25 had excessive late-onset depression and remitted patients). Sites with fewer than 10 MDD patients or 10 HC subjects were also excluded. The final sample comprised 1619 participants (797 MDD, 822 HC).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "These data were obtained from a publicly accessible dataset from the REST-meta-MDD project (Yan et al., 2019) provided by the DIRECT consortium (Chen et al., 2022). Site 4 and Site 25 were excluded since Site 4's participants were duplicated with those from Site 14, and Site 25 contained an excessive number of late-onset depression cases (age > 60 years) and remitted patients."

answer.REST-meta-MDD (HC subset): normative model training and 10-fold cross-validation testing

answer.REST-meta-MDD (MDD subset): clinical application (individual deviation analysis, subtype classification via k-means clustering)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The HC subset (N=822) was used to build normative models of degree centrality via hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) with 10-fold cross-validation for model evaluation, then all HC data were used to train the final normative model. The MDD subset (N=797) was applied to the trained normative model to quantify individual deviations (z-scores) and to identify subtypes via k-means clustering.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "To evaluate the generalizability of the normative models, we first performed normative modeling on the HC using 10-fold cross-validation... Then, the normative models were trained on all HC data and later applied to MDD patients."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was constructed using hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) for each of the 96 brain regions. During 10-fold cross-validation evaluation, approximately 740 HC were used for training and 82 for testing in each fold. The final normative model was trained on all 822 HC before being applied to MDD patients. A validation model using the AAL90 atlas was also constructed following the same procedure, but the primary model used the Harvard-Oxford atlas.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Mean and SD are directly reported for the HC group (N=822). Min and max are inferred from the exclusion criteria (age < 18 years or > 65 years were excluded). The supplementary Figure S1 confirms the age distribution spans approximately 18-65 years. Since the final normative model was trained on all 822 HC, the train-phase statistics equal the overall-phase statistics.
